verses.text: A man named Lazarus was ill. He lived in Bethany, the village where Mary and her sister Martha lived.
This Mary was the one who later poured perfume on the Lord and wiped his feet with her hair. It was her brother Lazarus who was ill.
So the sisters sent a message to Jesus: "Lord, the one you love is ill."
When Jesus heard this, he said, "This illness will not end in death. It has happened for the glory of God, so that the Son of God will be honoured through it."
Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.
Yet when he heard that Lazarus was ill, he stayed where he was for two more days.
Then he said to his followers, "Let us go back to Judea."
"But Rabbi," they said, "only a short time ago the Jewish leaders there tried to stone you. Are you going back there?"
Jesus answered, "Are there not twelve hours of daylight? Anyone who walks during the day will not stumble, because they can see by the light of this world.
But anyone who walks at night will stumble, because they have no light."
After he had said this, he went on to tell them, "Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going there to wake him up."
His followers replied, "Lord, if he is sleeping, he will get better."
Jesus had been speaking about his death, but they thought he meant ordinary sleep.
So then he told them plainly, "Lazarus is dead.
For your sake I am glad that I was not there, because now you will believe. But let us go to him."
Then Thomas (also called the Twin) said to the other followers, "Let us go too, so that we may die with him."
When Jesus arrived, he found that Lazarus had already been in the tomb for four days.
Bethany was less than three kilometres from Jerusalem,
and many Jewish people had come to Martha and Mary to comfort them about the death of their brother.
When Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went out to meet him, but Mary stayed at home.
Martha said to Jesus, "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.
But I know that even now God will give you whatever you ask."
Jesus told her, "Your brother will rise again."
Martha answered, "I know he will rise again in the resurrection on the last day."
Jesus said to her, "I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me will live, even though they die.
And everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?"
"Yes, Lord," she replied. "I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God, the one who was to come into the world."
After she had said this, she went back and called her sister Mary aside. "The Teacher is here," she said, "and he is asking for you."
When Mary heard this, she got up quickly and went to him.
Jesus had not yet come into the village. He was still at the place where Martha had met him.
The Jewish people who had been with Mary in the house, comforting her, saw how quickly she got up and went out. So they followed her, thinking she was going to the tomb to cry there.
When Mary reached the place where Jesus was and saw him, she fell at his feet. She said, "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died."
When Jesus saw her crying, and saw the people who had come with her crying too, he was deeply moved in his spirit and greatly troubled.
"Where have you laid him?" he asked. "Come and see, Lord," they replied.
Jesus wept.
Then the people said, "See how much he loved him!"
But some of them said, "He opened the eyes of the blind man. Could he not have kept this man from dying?"
Jesus, once more deeply moved, came to the tomb. It was a cave with a stone placed across the entrance.
"Take away the stone," he said. Martha, the sister of the dead man, said, "But Lord, by now there will be a bad smell. He has been dead for four days."
Jesus said to her, "Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?"
So they took away the stone. Then Jesus looked up and said, "Father, thank you for hearing me.
I know that you always hear me. But I said this for the sake of the people standing here, so that they will believe that you sent me."
After he had said this, Jesus called out in a loud voice, "Lazarus, come out!"
The dead man came out. His hands and feet were wrapped with strips of cloth, and a cloth was wrapped around his face. Jesus said to them, "Unwrap him and let him go."
Many of the Jewish people who had come to visit Mary saw what Jesus did, and they believed in him.
But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.
Then the chief priests and the Pharisees called a meeting of the council. "What are we going to do?" they asked. "This man is doing many miraculous signs.
If we let him carry on like this, everyone will believe in him. Then the Romans will come and take away both our temple and our nation."
One of them, Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, spoke up. "You know nothing at all!" he said.
"You do not realise that it is better for you that one man should die for the people than for the whole nation to be destroyed."
He did not say this on his own. As high priest that year, he was speaking God's message without knowing it: Jesus would die for the Jewish nation,
and not only for that nation, but also to bring together all of God's children who were scattered everywhere, and make them one.
So from that day on they made plans to kill Jesus.
For this reason Jesus no longer moved about openly among the Jewish people. Instead, he went to a region near the desert, to a village called Ephraim, and stayed there with his followers.
It was nearly time for the Jewish Passover festival. Many people went up from the countryside to Jerusalem before the Passover to make themselves ceremonially clean.
They kept looking for Jesus. As they stood in the temple courts, they asked one another, "What do you think? Is he coming to the festival at all?"
But the chief priests and the Pharisees had given orders that anyone who found out where Jesus was must report it, so that they could arrest him.
